interface.routine_auth: DM-scoped bearer with live Silicon Accounts introspection

production_browser: Chromium on a separate origin reads the guide, contract, inbox, contacts, people and requests with a DM bearer and zero cookies.
The standalone interface reaches upload configuration and an authenticated upload-status lookup.
A CORS-preflighted preference write round-tripped and the original setting was restored.
Saving an alias, note, trust and private photo in the native form created the same record in Silicon Contacts.
An edit in Silicon Contacts reappeared in DM with the private image. A fuzzy match selected the saved identity.
The native request inbox and direct-message setting rendered, and the contacts page fit a mobile viewport.
The production catalog points to the working public guide.
production_attachments: Different app access token refused by DM and uploads
Separate-origin browser uploaded and downloaded matching bytes through Briefcase
Temporary file moved to the owner bin
verification.browser_test_context: Separate-origin Chromium connected directly to production. Native form and mobile checks used the locally served release build against production with the shared Silicon identity.
verification.cross_service_test: Both HTTP services and PostgreSQL running locally. The Carbon opted into contacts-only DMs. A Silicon received a 409 and the Carbon saw a single request. Saving the Silicon in DM allowed the next message and was visible in Silicon Contacts. After acceptance, removing the contact preserved permission for the pair.
verification.presentation: All 30 documentation pages built and passed navigation, canonical link and machine-readable content checks.
verification.isolated_mutations: No production invitation or chat message sent. Temporary contacts were removed, attachment test files moved to the owner bin, and the original DM preference restored.

dependency_audit.status: Two findings predate this release. Both dependency versions are present on the production base branch.
